X research · 14 Nov 2026 · for Future Party 2050

The viral camera effects are hand tracking, not OpenCV filters

The futuristic webcam pieces spreading on X are a webcam, Google’s MediaPipe (21 points per hand) and a shader or TouchDesigner, often one HTML file written with an AI model. The three most-viewed turn your hands into glass or silk and reached 2.6 to 3.0 million views each. I rebuilt eight of these effects as Mirror 2050, a single-page camera mirror for the party that runs at 60 fps.

Open Mirror 2050 → serve this folder first: python3 -m http.server 8050 -d mirror

What the search found

Counts are from the 18 posts in the table below.

14/18

MediaPipe does the work, OpenCV mostly doesn’t

Fourteen posts track hands, heads or bodies with MediaPipe or its 21-point hand model. Only one names OpenCV: a red-cloth invisibility cloak from 2020 (1.5k likes). Today OpenCV trends in sports analysis instead: a YOLO + OpenCV football tracker drew 1.08M views.

3

The biggest reach is your hand becoming a material

The three most-viewed posts (3.0M, 2.8M, 2.6M) all turn the hand into silk or glass that moves with it.

what if air had a surface
built with WebGL shaders + MediaPipe hand tracking
single HTML file, no app, no install@xbh_artist, 21 May 2026
5.8M

Retellings carry the largest numbers

Both silk posts reuse a TouchDesigner clip made by someone else, with copy that sets it against Apple’s Vision Pro. Together they have 5.8M views; the maker of the clip is not named in either.

Just a webcam, TouchDesigner and a kid who saw the Vision Pro keynote and thought, I can do that for free.@defileo, 1 May 2026
3

The AI model is part of the hook

Three posts name an AI model next to the stack (Opus 4.5, Claude, Gemini 3), and the particle-text author posted the whole prompt as a reply.

Opus 4.5 + three.js + mediapipe = Absolute Cinema@V7700SN, 10 Jan 2026 · 8.6k likes
13.6k

The most-liked effect leaves the screen

A webcam watches a wall and a projector throws balls that bounce off real sticky notes. It has the most likes of any effect here, though fewer views (874k) than the hand pieces.

Mirror 2050, the mini-app

One HTML file in the party repo, mirror/index.html. Screenshots from headless Chrome with a viral clip as the camera, so parts of the clip’s own overlay show through (the blue cube in some frames).

Run it at the party

# from the future-party repo
python3 -m http.server 8050 -d mirror
open http://localhost:8050          # Chrome or Edge

# projector: camera on, controls hidden, new effect every 25 s
open "http://localhost:8050/?party"

# offline laptop: run once while online (26 MB, not committed)
mirror/tools/vendor.sh

The camera needs localhost or https. Frames stay in the browser: they go to the GPU and to MediaPipe in the same tab. With no hand tracking available, every effect still runs on its own.

1 – 8switch effect · ← → previous, next Hhand HUD: skeleton, fingertip reticles, palm ring, pinch distance in mm Aparty mode Ssave a snapshot as PNG Cnext camera (for an external webcam) Mmirror on or off BCloak: learn the empty room again Ithe sources, inside the app
  • Tested: all eight effects at 60 fps in headless Chrome 157, hands tracked in about 11 ms per frame on the GPU, through a fake camera and from a video file, with tracking on and off, and with MediaPipe loaded from vendor/.

Not checked, or uncertain

  • X only, through its search (Top results, with like thresholds). TikTok, Instagram and YouTube were not searched, and posts below the thresholds were not seen.
  • Likes and views were read on 14 Nov 2026 and keep changing.
  • The silk clip’s original maker was not found. Claims in the retelling posts (fees per event, “crashed the stocks of Figma and Photoshop”) were not checked; only the stack and the numbers were used.
  • Mirror 2050 has not yet run with a live person in front of a real webcam, in Safari or Firefox, or on the projector laptop. Gesture thresholds (open palm, fist, pinch) may need tuning there.
  • Cloak needs to see the room without you once; until then it fills the gap from the edges, which looks smeared.
